findings.title: backupCodes state typed as never[]
findings.body: `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([])` infers `never[]`, so `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` and `backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode)` are type errors (and `code` in the render map is `never`). This will break the TypeScript build / requires implicit any. Should be `useState<string[]>([])`.

findings.title: Download button inside <Form> can submit the form
findings.body: The "download" Button is rendered inside the `<Form handleSubmit={handleEnable}>` element and, unlike the adjacent close/copy buttons, does not call `e.preventDefault()`. If the button resolves to type="submit" it will re-trigger `handleEnable` (another /enable API call with a stale/empty totpCode) while also performing the download, producing an unexpected error state. Give it `type="button"` (or preventDefault and trigger the download programmatically).

findings.title: Object URL for backup codes is never revoked on unmount/close
findings.body: `URL.createObjectURL` is only revoked when a new setup is started. Closing the dialog or unmounting leaves the blob (containing plaintext backup codes) alive in memory for the page lifetime. Revoke it in a cleanup effect / in resetState.

findings.title: Used backup code replaced with null, leaving JSON nulls in array
findings.body: Setting `backupCodes[index] = null` re-encrypts an array containing nulls. The stored type is then `(string|null)[]`, which breaks the invariant assumed by other consumers (e.g. disable.ts parses and indexOf's the same array) and makes it impossible to distinguish 'used' from 'never generated'. Consider storing a sentinel string or filtering/regenerating consistently and typing the parsed value.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is not atomic (race allows reuse)
findings.body: The code is verified from a read copy and the remaining codes are written back with a plain `update`. Two concurrent login attempts with the same backup code both read the same array, both succeed, and the second write overwrites the first, so a single-use code can be used more than once. Use a conditional/transactional update (e.g. transaction with re-read, or update guarded by the previous backupCodes value) to make consumption atomic.

findings.title: Unvalidated req.body.backupCode can throw 500
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes a string. A client sending a number/object/array for `backupCode` passes the truthiness check and then throws a TypeError, returning an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. Validate the body type (e.g. zod) before use.

findings.title: Backup codes persisted at setup time even if 2FA is never enabled
findings.body: The setup endpoint writes `backupCodes` while `twoFactorEnabled: false`. If the user abandons the flow, stale codes remain stored; each repeated setup silently invalidates previously shown codes. Consider persisting the codes only when 2FA is actually enabled, or documenting/clearing the abandoned state.

findings.title: "Lost access" toggle button lacks type="button"
findings.body: This Button is inside `<Form form={form} handleSubmit={handleDisable}>`. If it is rendered as a submit button it will submit the disable form (with empty code) when the user just wants to switch to the backup-code input, showing a spurious error. Explicitly set `type="button"` to be safe.

findings.title: Clipboard assertion likely flaky in headless browsers
findings.body: The test clicks the copy button and waits for a success toast, but `navigator.clipboard.writeText` requires clipboard-write permission and a focused document; in headless CI it can reject, so the toast never appears and the test fails intermittently. Grant clipboard permissions via the browser context or skip this assertion.

findings.title: Component exported as `TwoFactor` in BackupCode.tsx
findings.body: The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`, which is misleading in stack traces/devtools and when debugging the login flow where both components are rendered. Rename to `BackupCode`.
